messages.subject: Re: Problem: CFA with one general factor and two additional factors (lavaan WARNINGS)
parts:
On 04/05/2013 11:42 AM, dom...@gmx.de wrote:

> Why does this happen? I am very grateful for your help.

The 'general' (g) and 'specific' (f1,f2) factors should be uncorrelated.
This explains the warning why lavaan could not compute the standard
errors. But my own attempt (see below) still resulted in a negative
variance. In this case, it is surely a symptom of model
misspecification, since we know that the data has been generated from an
ordinary two-factor model.

Yves.


# my attempt
model <- ' f1 =~ u1 + u2 + u3
f2 =~ u4 + u5 + u6
g =~ u1 + u2 + u3 + u4 + u5 + u6
g ~~ 0*f1 + 0*f2
'

# fit model
fit <- cfa(model, data=Data, verbose=TRUE, std.lv=TRUE)
